title: Greifswald Registry for Intracranial Hemorrhage under chronic medication in Neurosurgery
summary: In this registry study, patients with a brain hemorrhage under long-term medication are recorded and followed up for three months. After four, eight, and twelve weeks, the current health status and any impairments are assessed via telephone, as well as the current medication, with particular attention to medications affecting blood coagulation. If such blood-thinning medications are being taken, the exact time after the occurrence of the brain hemorrhage should be recorded to determine whether there is a temporal connection with any subsequent (re)bleeding or vascular occlusions (thromboses/embolisms). This aims to draw conclusions about when it is safe to resume a previously existing blood-thinning regimen without causing a recurrent organ bleeding.

interventions.name: Observational study. Patients with intracranial hemorrhages are monitored regarding their medication and clinical-radiological status on the day of admission (NIHSS, ICH score, GCS) and at 4, 8, and 12 weeks (t1-t3) (mRS, KPS, GOS).
